title: fix: HLS.js fallback for video playback in media preview
body:
## Summary

- some uploaded videos fail to play in Chrome's native `<video>` decoder. divine-web already handles this with HLS.js fallback to transcoded segments — the admin UI didn't have it.
- adds `HlsVideo` component: tries native MP4 first, falls back to HLS.js (`media.divine.video/{hash}/hls/master.m3u8`), then to the authenticated media proxy for gated content
- distinguishes "content not available" (404/deleted) from "failed to load" (other errors) in the media preview UI
- fixes the `showByDefault` race condition where media would flash-show then collapse as report priority data loaded (tri-state `hasHighPriorityReports`)
- adds `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` to worker CORS headers (required for the credentialed media proxy fetch). `credentials: include` is scoped to the two media-proxy fetches only — no other API calls are affected

## Test plan

- [ ] open a report with video content at relay.admin.divine.video — videos that previously showed as black rectangles with inactive controls should now play via HLS
- [ ] open a report with image content — images still load normally
- [ ] open a report with a high-priority category — media should start hidden
- [ ] open a report with a non-high-priority category — media should start visible
- [ ] verify no CORS errors in browser console on report list or report detail pages
- [ ] verify deleted/unavailable media shows "Content not available" (ImageOff icon) instead of generic warning triangle

title: feat(auto-hide): configurable tiers, settings UI, media proxy fixes
body:
## Summary

- **Auto-hide settings UI** — new `AutoHideSettings` component in the Settings tab for configuring auto-hide tiers (Immediate + Threshold), trusted clients, categories, and thresholds. Uses `getApiHeaders()` for CF Access auth.
- **ReportWatcher tier-aware auto-hide** — `processAutoHide` now reads tier config from DO storage, routes reports to immediate (single trusted-client report) or threshold (N unique reporters per category) processing paths. Threshold counting is category-scoped via exact `reason` match in D1.
- **Media proxy hardening** — fixes a dead-end state where proxy-fetched content that isn't renderable (e.g. non-video blob) caused a permanent black frame instead of falling back to the broken-media icon. Adds `key={displayUrl}` to force remount when proxy URL arrives.
- **QUARANTINE recognized as blocked** — `useMediaStatus` now treats `QUARANTINE` (moderation-service D1 action) as a blocked state, so the action bar correctly shows "Unblock Media" instead of "Block Media & Ban Event" for quarantined items.
- **Pending review filters** — auto-hide actions excluded from resolved targets so auto-hidden items appear in the pending review queue. Category filter cleared when toggling pending review on.
- **BLOSSOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET** binding added to prod and staging wrangler configs (Secrets Store).
- **Blob URL cleanup** on unmount for `InlineMediaPreview` (memory leak fix).

## What changed (by area)

### Worker (Durable Object)
- `ReportWatcher.ts`: tier-aware `processAutoHide`, category-scoped `countUniqueReporters`, config GET/PUT endpoints, `isAlreadyAutoHidden` deduplication
- `ReportWatcher.test.ts`: 163 tests covering immediate/threshold tiers, trusted client gating, config validation, deduplication
- `index.ts`: forward request body to DO for PUT /config

### Frontend
- `AutoHideSettings.tsx`: new settings UI with chip lists for categories/clients, tier config, client-side validation
- `MediaPreview.tsx`: proxy blob recovery, blob URL cleanup, `key={displayUrl}` remount
- `useMediaStatus.ts`: QUARANTINE recognized as blocked
- `Reports.tsx`: auto-hide actions excluded from resolved, category filter cleared on pending review toggle
- `SettingsDashboard.tsx`: mounts `AutoHideSettings`

### Config
- `wrangler.prod.toml`, `wrangler.staging.toml`: BLOSSOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET secrets store binding

## Test plan

- [x] Deploy to staging (test instance), verify auto-hide settings load and save
- [x] Trigger threshold-tier auto-hide with 2 reports from different pubkeys, same category — confirm event is hidden
- [x] Verify single cross-category report does NOT trigger threshold (category scoping)
- [x] Confirm CSAM/immediate tier fires on single trusted-client report
- [ ] Open a report with quarantined media — verify "Unblock Media" button appears (not "Block Media & Ban Event")
- [ ] Verify media proxy shows broken icon (not black frame) when proxy content is unrenderable
- [ ] Verify pending review toggle shows auto-hidden items, not resolved items

title: ci: ReportWatcher health check with self-healing
body:
## Summary
- Polls staging + production ReportWatcher every 15 min
- Auto-restarts via `/api/report-watcher/start` if unhealthy, re-checks after 30s
- Alerts `#divine-alerts` via Slack webhook only after 2+ consecutive post-recovery failures
- `continue-on-error: true` prevents workflow failure notifications to repo watchers

Closes divinevideo/support-trust-safety#130 -- Structured diagnostic output distinguishing auth errors (HTTP 401/403), timeouts (curl exit 28), DNS failures, connection refused, and JSON parse errors.

Closes divinevideo/support-trust-safety#131 -- Replaced actions/cache with GitHub Actions repo variables (`RW_FAILS_STAGING`, `RW_FAILS_PRODUCTION`). Simple integers, no cache accumulation, inspectable and resettable from Settings UI.

## Setup (before enabling)
Add three repo secrets (Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions):
- `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` -- Cloudflare Access service token (same as support-trust-safety)
- `CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET` -- same
- `SLACK_WEBHOOK_ALERTS` -- Incoming webhook for #divine-alerts (same value as `vmalertmanager-slack-webhook-production` in GCP Secret Manager, ask Sam/Ira)

Repo variables (`RW_FAILS_STAGING`, `RW_FAILS_PRODUCTION`) are created automatically on first run.

Workflow runs harmlessly without secrets (curl fails, Slack step skips with warning, workflow stays green).

## Context
Replaces the version in support-trust-safety. Lives here because ReportWatcher is a Cloudflare Durable Object outside the GKE observability perimeter -- no Prometheus, VMRule, or liveness probe can reach it.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge and configure secrets
- [ ] Run manually from Actions tab to verify staging/prod checks
- [ ] Verify Slack message format in #divine-alerts
- [ ] Stop ReportWatcher manually, confirm auto-restart works
- [ ] Confirm no email notifications to repo watchers on failure

title: fix: add blob: to media-src CSP for proxied video previews
body:
## Summary

Adds `blob:` to the `media-src` CSP directive in `index.html`. Proxied restricted media creates blob URLs that `media-src 'self' https:` was blocking. `img-src` and `connect-src` already allow `blob:` -- this aligns `media-src`.

## Motivation

Restricted video content loads through the admin media proxy (`/api/media-proxy/{sha256}`), which fetches from the media server's admin endpoint and creates a blob URL for the `<video>` element. CSP was blocking the blob URL, causing the AlertTriangle fallback instead of the video preview.

title: feat: send DM notifications on ban and report-queue delete via moderation-service
body:
Recreated from #39 (closed due to branch ref issue during rebase).

## Summary

- Ban and report-queue delete actions now send NIP-17 DMs to affected users via moderation-service's `/api/v1/notify` endpoint
- Ban actions use ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED template; event deletions use PERMANENT_BAN
- DM sending is a non-critical side effect -- failures are logged, never block the moderation response

## Scope

DMs are sent on these paths:
- **Ban user** via `banpubkey` RPC (the path all UI components use) and the `ban_pubkey` moderate action (API-only, not called from UI)
- **Standalone event delete** from the reports queue (has reported user pubkey from report context)
- **Block-and-delete** from the reports queue (same)

DMs are intentionally NOT sent on:
- **Event deletions during user bans** -- the ban itself sends a DM, omitting pubkey here avoids duplicates
- **BulkDeleteByKind, EventDetail, useAdminPublish** -- no pubkey context available. Edge cases to revisit if not superseded by osprey/coop

## Changes

- `notifyModerationService()` helper calls moderation-service's `/api/v1/notify` via CF Access auth
- Wired into `handleRelayRpc()` for `banpubkey` method (the actual UI ban path)
- Wired into `handleModerate()` for `ban_pubkey` and `delete_event` actions
- Frontend `deleteEvent()` passes author pubkey for report-queue deletions so the worker can notify the creator

## Test plan

- [x] 71 tests passing, tsc clean
- [ ] Deploy both services to staging
- [ ] Ban a test user in relay admin, verify DM arrives with account suspension message
- [ ] Delete a test event from reports queue, verify DM arrives with content removal message
- [ ] Dismiss a report, verify no DM is sent

Relates to support-trust-safety#65, support-trust-safety#101

title: feat: add age-restrict media action to relay admin UI
body:
## Summary

Three improvements to the relay admin moderation workflow, deployed and tested together:

1. **Age Restrict action + service binding auth fix** -- new UI option alongside Block Media, plus fixes to handleModerateMedia() which never worked in production due to hostname routing and auth issues
2. **REST report fetching** -- replaces stale browser WebSocket queries with server-side relay queries through the worker
3. **Report detail stability** -- fixes full-page reloads during background data refreshes

## Age Restrict + Auth Fix

- useMediaStatus hook distinguishes blocked (PERMANENT_BAN) from restricted (AGE_RESTRICTED) with separate flags
- New "Age Restrict" button (orange) with confirmation dialog. "Remove Restriction" when already restricted.
- Decision log records restrict_media/unrestrict_media as distinct actions
- No backend changes -- handleModerateMedia() already accepted AGE_RESTRICTED

handleModerateMedia() never worked in production. Root cause was three layered issues:
- moderation-service enforces hostname/path routing: /api/* paths only work on moderation-api.divine.video, not moderation.admin.divine.video
- moderation-api.divine.video has no CF Access edge, so service token headers weren't processed into a JWT
- No Bearer token was configured for direct auth

Fix: added MODERATION_API service binding to divine-moderation-service (bypasses CF Access + network). Bearer token auth via SERVICE_API_TOKEN for service binding requests.

**Post-action verification (f40afbe):** Added verifyAgeRestricted() with a 1-second delay before rechecking status, matching the existing verifyMediaBlocked() pattern. The age-restrict mutation's onSuccess now shows verification toasts (confirmed/warning) instead of silently assuming success. Companion fix: divine-moderation-service#57 returns 502 when the Blossom webhook fails, so the relay admin no longer shows success when enforcement didn't land.

Closes a vocabulary alignment gap (support-trust-safety#101, divine-moderation-service#51).

## REST Report Fetching

Browser's nostrify NPool WebSocket served stale cached data -- newly published reports didn't appear until page reload. Relay returns correct data (verified via nak), but client-side connection cached results.

- Worker: two new GET endpoints (/api/reports, /api/resolution-labels) using existing queryRelay() with fresh WebSocket per request
- Frontend: swapped queryFns from nostr.query() to REST calls through worker

## Report Detail Stability

- Added placeholderData and retry:false to all polling queries
- Detail pane holds selected report in state independently of list data refreshes
- Background polling updates the list without disrupting the detail view or closing modals
- Fixed production build crash (temporal dead zone in minified bundle)

## Tested

- 75 worker tests, 57 API client tests passing
- Build clean, tsc clean
- Age-restrict action shows verification toast confirming restriction landed
- Moderation-service 502 on Blossom failure propagates as error toast
- Reports load fresh on each poll
- Detail pane stays stable during 15s background refetches

Closes divine-moderation-service#51
Relates to support-trust-safety#101, support-trust-safety#119, divine-moderation-service#57

## Summary

Consolidates the three stacked PRs (#18 CSAM auto-hide, #29 Funnelcake REST reads, #28 ban-user-delete) into a single branch on top of current main. Incorporates Liz's bug fixes from #31 and adds a deeper fix for the query key mismatch.

### What's included

**From PR #18 (CSAM auto-hide):**
- ReportWatcher Durable Object for auto-hide on first CSAM report
- Zendesk bi-directional sync (pre-auth, JWT, ticket lifecycle)
- NIP-98 auth on mobile JWT endpoint

- Human decision persistence (moderation_targets table)

**From PR #29 (Funnelcake REST reads):**
- Funnelcake REST API proxy for faster event/user lookups
- Thread context with external relay hint fetching
- Moderation status consolidation (unified useModerationStatus hook)
- Decision logging for bulk delete and dismiss
- CSS overflow fixes for narrow viewports
- Graceful failure states and loading indicators

**From PR #28 (Rabble's ban-user-delete):**
- Always delete the reported event when banning a user
- Include reported event's media when blocking media

### Liz's bug fixes integrated (#31)

All three fixes from Liz's PR are incorporated:

1. **Profile loading** -- NostrProvider indexer relay fan-out (purplepag.es, relay.damus.io, user.kindpag.es) kept from main. Complementary with the Funnelcake REST approach in useAuthor.
2. **Report count flickering** -- placeholderData + retry on the decisions query in Reports.tsx.
3. **Dismissed reports reappearing** -- root cause fix (see below) replaces the 10-location symptom patch.

### Query key unification (root cause fix)

Reports.tsx used `['all-decisions']` while ReportDetail.tsx used `['decisions']` for the same `getAllDecisions()` API call. Cache invalidation after moderation actions only hit `['decisions']`, so the reports list never updated. Unified to a single `['decisions']` key everywhere, eliminating the mismatch instead of patching every invalidation site.

### Test fixes

Fixed 4 pre-existing test failures:
- ReportWatcher: mock DB used wrong variable name (`sql` instead of `_sql`), causing dedup and human-resolution mock checks to return wrong values
- adminApi: header assertions used exact match but didn't account for CF Access service token headers added since tests were written

title: fix: three content moderation queue bugs reported by T&S team
body:
Closes the three bugs Aleysha reported that are blocking content moderation work.

## Summary

### Bug 1 (HIGHEST): Report links not pulling full profile info
- **Problem**: Reported users showed as blank boxes with default names because `NostrProvider` only queried the Divine relay for kind 0 profiles. Users with nazi-themed usernames/profiles on other relays appeared harmless.
- **Fix**: Fan out kind 0 queries to indexer relays (`purplepag.es`, `relay.damus.io`, `user.kindpag.es`) alongside the configured relay. Increased `useAuthor` timeout from 1.5s to 5s.
- **Files**: `NostrProvider.tsx`, `useAuthor.ts`

### Bug 2: Report count flickering to 0 every ~30s
- **Problem**: `getAllDecisions` query caught errors and returned `[]`, which emptied `resolvedTargets`, causing the filtered list to briefly show 0 reports.
- **Fix**: Use `placeholderData` (stale-while-revalidate) to keep showing previous data during refetch errors. Added `retry: 2`. Removed the try/catch that swallowed errors.
- **File**: `Reports.tsx`

### Bug 3: Dismissed reports reappearing
- **Problem**: `ReportDetail` invalidated query key `['decisions']` after dismissal, but `Reports` uses `['all-decisions']` — completely different keys, so React Query never invalidated the reports list's cache.
- **Fix**: Added `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['all-decisions'] })` alongside every existing `['decisions']` invalidation (10 locations).
- **File**: `ReportDetail.tsx`

## Test plan
- [ ] Report a user from a non-Divine client (profile on purplepag.es only) → verify name/avatar loads in relay manager
- [ ] Dismiss a report → verify it does NOT reappear on next refresh
- [ ] Watch the report count during periodic refreshes → verify it stays stable (no flickering to 0)

title: feat: Funnelcake REST API reads for faster report loading
body:
## Stack

1. [PR #18: CSAM auto-hide, moderator safety, Zendesk integration](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/pull/18) -> `main`
2. **This PR (#29)** -> PR #18
3. [PR #28: Always delete reported event on ban](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-relay-manager/pull/28) -> this PR

---

## Summary

Faster report loading via Funnelcake REST API, UX overhaul for the report detail view, consolidated moderation status checking, and CSS overflow fixes. Everything deployed to production.

### Funnelcake REST API Reads

Worker proxy routes (`/api/funnelcake/event/{id}`, `/api/funnelcake/users/{pubkey}`) forward to Funnelcake's ClickHouse-backed REST API. Frontend hooks use REST first with automatic WebSocket fallback.

- Worker proxy: URL derivation (wss->https), cache header forwarding. 6 tests.
- API client: fetchFunnelcakeEvent(), fetchFunnelcakeUser(). 6 tests.
- useThread: REST -> local WS -> external relay hint (3-tier fetch)
- useAuthor: REST -> WS fallback
- apiUrl wired through useReportContext -> ThreadContext -> ThreadModal -> PostCard

### External Relay Hint Fetching

When REST and local WS both return nothing, useThread checks the report's e tag for a relay hint and tries a one-shot WebSocket fetch from that external relay (5s timeout). Applied to main event, repost originals, and ancestors.

### Report Detail UX

- Graceful loading: animated barber-pole progress bar replaces skeleton placeholders
- Staged messages: "Searching for reported content (including wss://relay.example.com/)..." -> "Checking moderation status..." -> terminal result
- Kind-aware headings: "Reported Video" / "Reported Comment" / "Reported Note"
- "External relay" badge when content fetched from outside our relay
- "No profile published to this relay" indicator
- Inline expand/collapse for long content (replaces dead links)
- "View on Divine" links on ancestor PostCards
- User reports show contextual investigation helpers message instead of misleading "content not found"

### Consolidated Moderation Status

Replaced three overlapping mechanisms (useModerationStatus ban list check, useBannedEvent admin API, manual checkLiveStatus WebSocket verify) with a single useModerationStatus hook:

- Auto-runs ban list queries (shared React Query cache)
- Auto-runs WebSocket verification when event not found via normal queries
- Auto-checks ban status for user reports (pubkey targets) on load
- Returns isUserBanned, isEventBanned, isEventGone, isChecking, checkedAt, recheck()
- recheck() for post-action verification

Removed the separate Live Moderation Status card. Status now displays inline in the reported content area (ThreadContext) with timestamp and re-check button. Single source of truth.

### Dismiss and Decision Logging Fixes

- Dismiss button always available regardless of event deletion status (was blocked when event deleted externally)
- Dismiss opens confirmation dialog with optional reason input (was hardcoded "no action needed")
- BulkDeleteByKind now logs delete_event decisions, accepts reason input, refreshes status on completion
- Decision log banner simplified to one-line last action + date

### CSS Overflow Fixes

Inspected live production via chrome-devtools-mcp at 1024px and 1440px viewports.

- Left pane: new TargetId component shows full bech32 IDs (npub/note) with CSS truncation and copy button, consistent for event and user reports
- Right pane: overflow-hidden on UserProfileCard flex containers, block display on npub code elements
- ScrollArea: [&>div>div]:!block overrides Radix display:table (root cause of content pushing wider than container)
- ThreadModal: break-all on post content for long URLs
- Sheet close button: z-50 + background for mobile overlap
- ReportTagsFallback relay hint: added missing truncation

### User Report Status Display

For pubkey-target reports (no ThreadContext), moderation status block renders before the Reported User card with ban status, timestamp, and re-check button.

title: perf: reduce report loading latency
body:
## Summary

Reports page was taking 10+ seconds to load report context (reporter profile, thread ancestors, user stats) due to serial relay queries and no caching between report views.

- **Batch ancestor fetching**: Replace serial parent-chasing loop in `useThread` with upfront NIP-10 tag extraction (root + reply markers) and a single batched relay query. Ancestors and replies now fetched in parallel via `Promise.all`.
- **Query caching**: Add `staleTime` to all report context hooks so switching between reports reuses cached data instead of re-fetching:
  - `useThread`: 1 min (thread context is stable)
  - `useAuthor`: 5 min (profiles rarely change)
  - `useUserStats`: 2 min (stats change slowly)
  - `useReportContext` reporter stats: 5 min (reporter history is stable)
- **Timeout/retry tuning**: `useAuthor` timeout 1500ms → 3000ms (relay latency was causing premature failures), retry 3 → 1 (most failures are missing profiles, not transient)

## What this does NOT change

- No changes to moderation actions, decision persistence, or any mutation paths
- No changes to data displayed (same ancestors, same stats, same profiles)
- No new dependencies

## Test plan

- [ ] Open reports page on staging, verify reports load noticeably faster
- [ ] Click between multiple reports, verify cached data appears instantly on revisit
- [ ] Verify thread ancestors still display correctly (root → parent → event order)
- [ ] Verify reporter profile and stats still render
- [ ] Check a report for a reply event (has NIP-10 root/reply tags) and a top-level event (no ancestors)
- [ ] Check a repost event (kind 6/16) still shows original event content

title: feat: Zendesk pre-auth token hardening
body:
## Summary

- Adds HMAC-SHA256 pre-auth token hardening to the Zendesk JWT endpoint
- New `/api/zendesk/pre-auth` endpoint: NIP-98 authenticated, issues nonce-bound HMAC-signed tokens with 5-minute TTL
- `/api/zendesk/mobile-jwt` now verifies pre-auth tokens and atomically consumes nonces (single-use, replay-proof)
- Accepts both GET and POST on mobile-jwt for Zendesk SDK compatibility
- Defense-in-depth: DB-level expiry check on nonce DELETE (`expires_at >= unixepoch()`)
- Generic error messages in catch blocks (no internal details leaked to clients)
- D1 migration `0003_zendesk_preauth_nonces` for nonce storage with expiry index
- `ensureSchemaOnce` added to pre-auth endpoint for safety on fresh D1 databases

## Known follow-ups

1. **Legacy unauthenticated npub path** — raw npub/hex pubkey tokens bypass pre-auth entirely (`index.ts:2267-2282`). Intentional for backward compat with current deployed app. Remove once mobile PR ships and old app versions are no longer in use. Should have a tracked issue with a deadline.
2. **Timing attack in webhook signature comparison** (pre-existing) — `verifyZendeskWebhook` uses `===` string comparison (`index.ts:1356-1358`) instead of constant-time `crypto.subtle.verify`. The new `hmacVerify` helper does it correctly. Migrate webhook verifier to use the same pattern.
3. **Integration tests for nonce replay prevention** — unit tests cover HMAC generation/verification, but no tests for the DB-side nonce consumption (already-consumed nonce returns 401, never-stored nonce returns 401). Add integration tests.
4. **Purpose string in error message** — `zendesk-preauth.ts:131` embeds `TOKEN_PURPOSE` in error string. Not returned to HTTP clients currently, but could leak if error forwarding changes.

## Test plan

- [x] Pre-auth token generation with NIP-98 auth
- [x] HMAC verification (correct secret, wrong secret, tampered payload, expired token)
- [x] Nonce single-use enforcement (DELETE RETURNING)
- [x] Legacy npub path still works (backward compat)
- [x] GET and POST both accepted on mobile-jwt
- [x] Deployed to production, tested end-to-end with divine-mobile

title: feat: prevent auto-hide from overriding human moderation decisions
body:
## Summary
- Adds `moderation_targets` table to track per-target state (`ever_human_reviewed`), separated from the append-only `moderation_decisions` audit log
- `hasHumanResolution()` check in ReportWatcher blocks auto-hide when a human has previously acted on a target — prevents abusive re-reporting from reversing moderator decisions
- `markHumanReviewed()` called from all 5 moderator action paths: UI decisions, moderate API (delete_event/ban_pubkey), publish resolution labels (kind 1985), Zendesk webhook, Zendesk admin
- Reopen flow (DELETE /api/decisions/:id) clears decisions but preserves `moderation_targets` row — human review status survives reopening

**Also in this PR:**
- Environment-aware deep links: Zendesk content report links now include `?env=staging` or `?env=production`, and the frontend auto-switches environment before loading report data (closes divinevideo/support-trust-safety#88)
- Fixed 19 pre-existing TypeScript errors (ApiResponse type, MockWebSocket signatures)
- Created `proxyJsonResponse()` to separate untyped proxy pass-throughs from typed `jsonResponse()`

Depends on #18. Replaces #21 (moved from fork to upstream).

## Deploy note
After first deploy to each environment, run one-time backfill to protect previously-reviewed targets:
```
wrangler d1 execute <db-name> --config <wrangler.toml> --command "INSERT INTO moderation_targets (target_id, target_type, ever_human_reviewed) SELECT DISTINCT target_id, target_type, 1 FROM moderation_decisions WHERE action != 'auto_hidden' ON CONFLICT(target_id) DO UPDATE SET ever_human_reviewed = 1;"
```
Without backfill, previously-reviewed targets won't be protected until a new human action writes the row.

## Test plan

- [x] Local integration test: seeded 5 events with different decision states on old code, deployed new code, ran backfill, verified correct behavior on re-reports
- [x] Backfill idempotency verified

- Adds `moderation_targets` table to track per-target state (`ever_human_reviewed`), separated from the append-only `moderation_decisions` audit log
- `hasHumanResolution()` check in ReportWatcher blocks auto-hide when a human has previously acted on a target — prevents abusive re-reporting from reversing moderator decisions
- `markHumanReviewed()` called from all 5 moderator action paths: UI decisions, moderate API (delete_event/ban_pubkey), publish resolution labels (kind 1985), Zendesk webhook, Zendesk admin
- Reopen flow (DELETE /api/decisions/:id) clears decisions but preserves `moderation_targets` row — human review status survives reopening

## Deploy note
After first deploy to each environment, run one-time backfill to protect previously-reviewed targets:
```
wrangler d1 execute <db-name> --config <wrangler.toml> --command "INSERT INTO moderation_targets (target_id, target_type, ever_human_reviewed) SELECT DISTINCT target_id, target_type, 1 FROM moderation_decisions WHERE action IN ('auto_hide_restored','auto_hide_confirmed','reviewed','dismissed','no-action','false-positive','delete_event','ban_pubkey','ban_user') ON CONFLICT(target_id) DO UPDATE SET ever_human_reviewed = 1;"
```
Without backfill, previously-reviewed targets won't be protected until a new human action writes the row.

## Test plan
- [x] 58 unit tests passing (ReportWatcher + handler integration tests)
- [x] Local integration test: seeded 5 events with different decision states on old code, deployed new code, ran backfill, verified correct behavior on re-reports
- [x] Backfill idempotency verified
- [ ] Deploy to staging, run backfill, verify with live data
- [ ] Deploy to production, run backfill

Closes divinevideo/support-trust-safety#69 (Gaps 2+3: human decision persistence)

title: Zendesk sync, realness service binding, and multi-environment support
body:
> ⚠️ **Merge Order:** This PR includes all commits from PR #8 (CORS wildcard support). Recommend merging this PR and closing #8 as superseded, OR merge #8 first then this one.

> **Note:** This branch has been deployed to production instances (frontend at relay.admin.divine.video, workers for all three environments) for over a week. Core moderation has been validated on the new production relay.

## Summary

This PR adds bi-directional Zendesk integration, fixes the realness API connectivity issue, and establishes multi-environment support for staging/production infrastructure.

## Features

- **Zendesk bi-directional sync**
  - `POST /api/zendesk/parse-report` webhook parses incoming content report tickets
  - Stores ticket↔event mappings in D1 `zendesk_tickets` table
  - Adds internal notes with deep links to relay admin
  - `syncZendeskAfterAction()` updates/auto-solves tickets on moderation actions

- **Realness API via service binding**
  - Bypasses CF Access 522 timeout issue with worker-to-worker calls
  - Uses `REALNESS` service binding to `divine-ai-detector`

- **Multi-environment support**
  - New staging worker (`api-relay-staging.divine.video`)
  - Environment URLs moved to `VITE_*` env vars (not committed to repo)
  - Environment selector supports Legacy/Staging/Production

- **CORS improvements**
  - Support for multiple origins with wildcard subdomains
  - Allows CF Pages preview deployments

## Fixes

- **Deep link race condition** — URL params were clearing before report lookup completed
- **Event deletion** — Now uses `banevent` RPC instead of NIP-09 (author-only)
- **Reopen reports** — Properly removes resolution labels from relay
- **Cache invalidation** — Events list refreshes after moderation actions
- **Banned events filtering** — Client-side filter prevents showing banned content

## Issues Addressed

**divine-relay-manager:**
- Fixes #12 — Deep linking support for reports
- Fixes #14 — Realness proxy 522 timeout
- Fixes #15 — Deep link race condition on mobile

**support-trust-safety:**
- Addresses divinevideo/support-trust-safety#32 — New staging/production environment (epic)
- Addresses divinevideo/support-trust-safety#43 — Relay admin moderation actions update Zendesk tickets
- Includes fixes from divinevideo/support-trust-safety#26 — Fix moderation actions (closed)

## Configuration

All Zendesk secrets are already configured on staging and prod workers:
- ✅ `ZENDESK_API_TOKEN`
- ✅ `ZENDESK_EMAIL`
- ✅ `ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN`
- ✅ `ZENDESK_WEBHOOK_SECRET`
- ✅ `ZENDESK_PARSE_REPORT_SECRET`

Zendesk webhook needs to be configured to point at prod worker after cutover.

## Test Plan

- [x] Zendesk parse-report webhook tested (Ticket #631)
- [x] Service binding deployed to staging + prod
- [ ] Re-verify E2E realness analysis
- [ ] Re-verify E2E Zendesk sync (after cutover)

## Summary

Enables the worker to accept requests from multiple origins with support for wildcard subdomain patterns.

**Changes:**
- `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env var accepts comma-separated list
- Supports exact-match origins (e.g., `https://app.example.com`)
- Supports wildcard subdomain patterns (e.g., `*.preview.pages.dev`)
- Deny-by-default if env var is missing
- Added `getAllowedOrigin()` helper function

**Example configuration:**
```
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://relay.admin.divine.video,*.divine-relay-manager.pages.dev
```

This allows Cloudflare Pages preview deployments to work without manually updating CORS settings for each preview URL.

title: feat: configurable relay endpoints, CORS wildcards, and deletion fix
body:
This PR combines several improvements to support deploying the relay manager against different relay environments (staging vs production) and fixes issues with event deletion
    and CORS for preview deployments.

   ### Features

   - **Configurable relay endpoints** - Deploy to different relays without code changes
     - Frontend: `VITE_RELAY_URL` env var (set in Cloudflare Pages dashboard)
     - Worker: `RELAY_URL`, `MANAGEMENT_PATH`, `MODERATION_SERVICE_URL` env vars
     - Supports Funnelcake relay's `/management` NIP-86 path

   - **CORS wildcard support** - Enable Cloudflare Pages preview deployments
     - `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` supports comma-separated list with wildcard subdomains
     - Example: `https://app.example.com,*.divine-relay-admin.pages.dev`

   - **Event deletion fix** - Call `banevent` RPC after publishing kind 5 deletion
     - Ensures deleted events appear in `listbannedevents`
     - Fixes "Event may still be accessible" verification warning

   ### Documentation

   - Added `DEPLOYMENT.md` with full configuration guide for both environments
   - Added `.env.example` for local development

   ### TypeScript/ESLint Fixes

   - Fixed type annotations throughout codebase
   - Removed unused imports and variables
   - Proper type casting in DebugPanel

title: fix: correct WORKER_URL default to use custom domain route
body:
Changes the default WORKER_URL from the non-functional workers.dev subdomain to the actual custom domain route where the worker is deployed.

Problem:
- Worker is deployed to relay.admin.divine.video/api/* route
- Frontend was calling divine-relay-admin-api.divine-video.workers.dev
- That URL doesn't resolve (worker not published to workers.dev)
- All moderation actions (block media, delete event, ban user) failed silently

Solution:
- Update default WORKER_URL to https://relay.admin.divine.video
- Matches the actual worker deployment route
- Works out-of-the-box for production
- Can still override with VITE_WORKER_URL env var

Impact:
- Fixes all moderation actions on production
- Block media, delete events, ban users now work
- No environment variable needed for production deployment
